findings.proposed: (none; no UN counterpart for parts marking)
findings.evidence: UN R162 is 'Immobilisers' (repo ece-r162 title: 'UN Regulation No. 162 — Immobilisers'). Part 541 requires VIN marking on major parts to trace stolen components, not immobilizer performance.

findings.proposed: (none)
findings.evidence: Part 542 is purely a procedure for manufacturers and NHTSA to select new light-duty truck lines likely to have high/low theft rates (542.1(a) 'procedures ... to follow in the determination of whether any new light duty truck line is likely to have a theft rate above or below the 1990/91 median'). R116 (unauthorised use protection) and R162 (immobilisers) are technical device requirements, not equivalent.

findings.proposed: (none)
findings.evidence: Part 545 is a one-time manufacturer reporting/recordkeeping requirement about Part 541 phase-in (545.6: 'Within 60 days after the end of the production year ending August 31, 2007'). No UN technical counterpart.

findings.proposed: none (R108/R109 cover retreaded tyres but not regrooving)
findings.evidence: Part 569 body: 'sets forth the conditions under which regrooved and regroovable tires ... may be sold'. UN R30 is new pneumatic tyres for passenger cars; no regrooving provisions.

findings.current: Summary describes only vehicles with GVWR of 10,000 lb or less
findings.proposed: Mention Subpart B (GVWR > 10,000 lb; brake, steering/suspension, tire/wheel inspection)

This part specifies standards and procedures for the inspection of brake, steering and suspension systems, and tire and wheel assemblies, of motor vehicles in use with a gross vehicle weight rating of more than 10,000 pounds.'

findings.proposed: add Heavy truck, Bus, Trailer

findings.proposed: Drop UN R16 (seat belts); UN R94/R95 only as loose related (they reference dummies, no UN equivalent of Part 572 itself)
findings.evidence: Part 572 body: 'This part describes the anthropomorphic test devices that are to be used for compliance testing... It does not in itself impose duties'. UN R16 is a seat-belt component regulation, not a dummy specification.

findings.proposed: UN R30/R54/R117 (tyre approval/marking) or none
findings.evidence: UN R142 'approval of motor vehicles with regard to the installation of their tyres'; Part 574 is tire identification (TIN) and purchaser recordkeeping for tire manufacturers/dealers, not vehicle tyre installation.

findings.proposed: (none)
findings.evidence: Part 588 is only an owner-registration recordkeeping duty: 'maintain lists of the names and addresses of child restraint owners' to support recall notification (s588.1, s588.2). UN R44/R129 are product performance approvals; no UN counterpart for recall recordkeeping.

findings.proposed: (none)
findings.evidence: s591.1: 'establishes procedures governing the importation of motor vehicles and motor vehicle equipment' (customs/declaration procedure). UN R116/R162 are anti-theft/immobilizer technical requirements; no UN equivalent for an import declaration procedure.

findings.proposed: (none)

findings.proposed: (none) or Body structure/Labels

findings.current: in-force (summary: manufactured on or after Sept 1, 2007)

findings.evidence: s575.301(b): 'manufactured on or after September 1, 2007 ... except for vehicles that are subject to s575.302' and title '(applicable unless a vehicle is subject to s575.302)'. 575.302 applies to MY2012+ built on/after Jan 31, 2012, so for current production 575.301 is superseded; summary does not say so.

findings.proposed: (remove; no direct UN regulation for windshield wiping/washing; EU equivalent is Directive 78/318/EEC, repealed into Reg. (EU) 2018/858 / 2021/535 framework)
findings.evidence: UN R45 is 'Headlamp cleaners'. Repo body S1: 'This standard specifies requirements for windshield wiping and washing systems.' (windshield wipers/washers, not headlamp cleaners)

findings.proposed: UN R13 only (R13H is for M1/N1 passenger-car-type vehicles; FMVSS 135 is its US counterpart)
findings.evidence: Repo body S3: 'applies to multi-purpose passenger vehicles, trucks, and buses with a GVWR greater than 3,500 kilograms'. UN R13-H applies to category M1 and N1 (<=3.5 t) vehicles, outside FMVSS 105 scope.

findings.proposed: (remove; R11 covers door latches and hinges, not hood latches)
findings.evidence: UN R11 is 'Door latches and door retention components'. Repo body S1: 'This standard establishes the requirement for providing a hood latch system'; S3: 'Hood means any exterior movable body panel forward of the windshield'. Record's own commodities include 'Door latches & hinges', which probably caused the mapping.

findings.proposed: UN R108 (retreaded pneumatic tyres for passenger cars and trailers; R109 for commercial vehicles)
findings.evidence: UN R30 covers NEW pneumatic tyres for passenger cars. Repo body S1: 'performance, labeling, and certification requirements for retreaded pneumatic passenger car tires'. UN R108 is 'Uniform provisions concerning the approval of the production of retreaded pneumatic tyres for motor vehicles and their trailers'.

findings.proposed: UN R54 (commercial vehicle tyres); add UN R75 for motorcycle tyres; drop R30
findings.evidence: Body S3(a): 'New pneumatic tires for ... GVWR of more than 4,536 kilograms'; also motorcycle tyres. UN R30 covers passenger-car (M1) tyres, outside FMVSS 119 scope (standard knowledge, not searched).

findings.proposed: UN R78 (L-category braking)
findings.evidence: Body: 'S1 ... performance requirements for motorcycle brake systems'; 'S3 applies to motorcycles'. UN R13 covers M/N/O heavy vehicle braking; R78 is the motorcycle braking regulation (standard knowledge, not searched).

findings.proposed: UN R60 (motorcycle/moped driver-operated controls and indicators)
findings.evidence: FMVSS 123 is motorcycle controls and displays ('S1 ... location, operation, identification, and illumination of motorcycle controls and displays'). UN R121 covers identification of controls/tell-tales for M and N vehicles; R60 is the L-category counterpart (from standard knowledge, not searched).

findings.proposed: Remove / no UN equivalent
findings.evidence: Body S1: 'devices that can be installed on school buses ... stop signal arm'. R150 is retro-reflecting devices and R148 is light-signalling devices; neither regulates school-bus stop arms. No UN counterpart known (standard knowledge, not searched).

findings.proposed: UN R13 (Annex 21, vehicle stability function) for M3/N3/O heavy vehicles; remove UN R140
findings.evidence: Record body S3 limits scope to 'Truck tractors with a gross vehicle weight rating of greater than 11,793 kilograms' and 'Buses with a gross vehicle weight rating of greater than 11,793 kilograms'. UN R140 (ESC) applies to light vehicles (M1, N1 up to 3.5 t, and M2/N2 not covered by R13), not heavy tractors/buses; the heavy-vehicle stability requirement is in UN R13 Annex 21. Based on repository text plus standard knowledge of UN R140 scope (not web-verified).

Title: 'Applicable at the manufacturers option until September 1, 2009.' Successor is 571.202a, mandatory from 1 Sept 2009. Section remains in the CFR but has no application to current new vehicles. findings.evidence: S1. Scope. This standard establishes windshield retention requirements for motor vehicles during crashes. (R43 is the glazing-material regulation, a different subject)

findings.proposed: adopted / not yet applicable (applies to child restraint systems manufactured on or after 2026-12-05)
findings.evidence: S3. Application. ... manufactured on or after December 5, 2026. (today is 2026-10-06; us-fmvss-213 S3: 'manufactured before December 5, 2026. FMVSS No. 213b applies to child restraint systems manufactured on or after December 5, 2026')

findings.proposed: none (no UN ejection-mitigation regulation); remove
findings.evidence: UN R95 is lateral collision protection; FMVSS 226 is ejection mitigation (side-window ejection impactor test/rollover). Body S2: applies to vehicles '4,536 kg or less' ... ejection of occupants through side windows. Not a counterpart.

findings.proposed: UN R118 (burning behaviour of interior materials)
findings.evidence: UN R21 covers interior fittings (head-impact/energy absorption), not flammability; the FMVSS 302 counterpart is UN R118 (also ISO 3795). Body: 'requires that these materials not burn or transmit a flame front ... exceeding 102 mm per minute'. Based on standard knowledge of UN R21/R118 scopes; no web check.

findings.proposed: UN R110 (CNG vehicle components/installation)
findings.evidence: UN R34 is fire-risk prevention for liquid-fuel vehicles; CNG vehicle fuel system is UN R110. Body S3: 'use CNG as a motor fuel'.

findings.proposed: UN R110 (CNG/LNG specific components; container requirements)
findings.evidence: UN R34 covers fire-risk prevention (liquid fuel tanks); CNG containers are covered by UN R110. Body S3: 'each container designed to store CNG as motor fuel on-board any motor vehicle'.

findings.proposed: UN R134 (hydrogen vehicle safety); related UN GTR 13
findings.evidence: R34 does not cover hydrogen systems; UN R134 is the hydrogen/fuel-cell vehicle regulation. Body S3: 'uses compressed hydrogen gas as a fuel source'.

findings.current: Lighting modules, Mirrors, Brakes, Glass, Seatbelts, Batteries, Horn
findings.proposed: Lighting modules, Mirrors, Brakes, Glass, Seatbelts
findings.evidence: Body S5(b) lists headlamps, turn/stop/tail lamps, reflectors, mirrors, parking brake, windshield (571.205), VIN, seat belts (571.209), rear visibility, and 'An alert sound as required by § 571.141'. No horn requirement exists; the alert sound is a pedestrian alert under FMVSS 141, not a horn. 'Batteries' appears only as a test condition (S6.3.6 state of charge), not an equipment requirement.

findings.proposed: (none/Materials & substances)
findings.evidence: Prop 65 is a chemical exposure warning law, not battery safety or vehicle emissions; body lists 'Materials, coatings, electronics, batteries, plastics, rubber, trim'.

findings.current: in-scope U.S. and EU companies conduct due diligence on regulated minerals used in vehicle electronics, batteries and components

findings.evidence: Regulation (EU) 2017/821 obligations fall on Union importers of 3TG minerals/metals, not on vehicle makers as such; cobalt/battery due diligence belongs to Battery Regulation (EU) 2023/1542, which the body itself lists under Related Regulations ('EU Battery Regulation due diligence'). Body says 'not a vehicle type-approval pass/fail test'.

findings.proposed: (none)

findings.proposed: (none)
